name: event-ring-chunk1236
note: Event ring, alt-enter fullscreen, delayed key-up, and the UI event view from d_event.cpp (1-273).
auditSeams: The ring is 128 slots. D_PostEvent drops a device change only when events[eventhead] is already a device change, before the dispatch callback. Dispatch returning true stores nothing. PostMouseMove scales by the sensitivity cvars, negates Y, then applies invertmousex and invertmouse, and posts only when a component is non-zero. Process on this Linux build toggles fullscreen for alt+Enter and for a GUI key-down of GK_RETURN with alt, then continues. WantEscape is called only for a key-down of KEY_ESCAPE, and a true result skips the console and the menu. GS_INTRO also skips those two. The game responder still runs, and a true result on a key-down marks that key. A later key-up of a marked key in the same pass is posted again after the pass. D_RemoveNextCharEvent requires a GUI key-down at the tail. It blanks GUI key-downs and the following GUI character, and it stops on any other GUI subtype. FInputEvent copies the low 8 bits of data1 into a one-character string, empty when that byte is 0. FUiEvent char events cast data1 to uint16 and encode it with the BMP UTF-8 rules. Mouse view coordinates truncate toward zero. The DEFINE_FIELD exports are the UiEvent and InputEvent names at the end of the file.
auditRationale: UNCredited d_event.cpp 1-273 (+273). The file ends at 273. A full tally line scan shows no overlap.
auditUncreditedRangeCheck: uncredited_range_check.py --file src/common/engine/d_event.cpp --start 1 --end 273 and a full tally line scan → no overlap.

A second device change is stored when the head slot is still empty. The drop looks at the slot about to be written. Alt+Enter flips fullscreen and skips the responders. Escape reaches the game responder only, and only when WantEscape returns true. A key-up is delayed only when that key was eaten earlier in the same pass. GS_INTRO skips the console and the menu. A failed GUI-keydown precondition is logged and does not walk the ring. Mouse coordinates truncate toward zero. A GUI character encodes its uint16 value as UTF-8.
